name: SikaBond PVA
paste:
SIKABOND® PVA: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaBond® PVA, November 2025, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sikabond_pva.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaBond® PVA where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2025, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. SikaBond® PVA is a cross linked waterbased adhesive suitable for interior and exterior applications. It is an ideal adhesive for bonding a wide range of timber components including tongue and groove, solid timber, laminated flooring and most porous substrates. SikaBond® PVA forms a tough permanent bond and makes it ideal for use by trades, carpenters and DIY.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaBond® PVA may be used on most porous substrates due to its excellent adhesion, including
    - Timber
    - MDF boards
    - Particle boards
    - Ply woods
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.2.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaBond® PVA
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Interior Exterior Wood Working Glue
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2025, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Excellent water resistance
    - High bond strength within 24 hours
    - Suitable for interior and exterior applications
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: White
    - Density: 1.0 ± 0.02 kg/l
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 250ml; 500ml; 1L; 5L
    - Shelf life: Twelve (12) months from its date of production
2.6 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions and out of direct sunlight at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C. Always refer to packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2025, Version 01.03) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (November 2025, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not use the SikaBond® PVA in applications under water pressure or permanent water immersion.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (November 2025, Version 01.03) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaBond® PVA, November 2025, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/e/sikabond_pva.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaBond® PVA, version 19/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sds-sikabond-pva.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Substrate preparation. For optimum adhesion the substrates must be clean, dry, sound and free from oils, grease, dust, loose or friable particles.
6.4 Ecology, health and safety - Application method / tools. SikaBond® PVA is supplied ready to use and applied by squeeze bottle, brush or roller. Bonds should be assembled within a few minutes and then tightly clamped or pressed until the adhesive has set. Wipe off any excess adhesive immediately after assembly with a dry or lightly damp cloth. Assemblies must be allowed to cure for a minimum of 24 hours prior to moving or transportation. Maximum bond strength is achieved within 48 hours. Allow floors 24 hours for the adhesive to cure prior to use.
6.5 Ecology, health and safety - Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use detergent and water.
6.6 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.7 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.8 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
